references.text: The continuation of the description of the hard labor imposed on the Israelites, using the same term 'בְּפָרֶךְ' (with harshness/oppression)
The Israelites groaned under slavery and cried out to God, showing the consequence of the harsh treatment described in 1:13
Pharaoh increases the labor burden on the Israelites, a continuation of the oppression that began in 1:13
God promises to deliver Israel from forced labor under the Egyptians, in response to the oppression in 1:13
The same Hebrew expression 'בְּפָרֶךְ' is used here in the law forbidding Israelites to rule over one another with harshness
Reiterates the prohibition against ruling with harshness ('בְּפָרֶךְ'), referencing the experience in Egypt
A confession text that recalls the Egyptians' oppression and the hard labor imposed on the Israelites
Ezekiel uses the same expression 'בְּפָרֶךְ' regarding rulers who treat the people with harshness, an echo of Egyptian oppression
Stephen's speech refers to how the Egyptians mistreated the ancestors of the Israelites, a direct reference to the events in Exodus 1
God confirms and responds to the oppression described in the source verse.
Theological application: The memory of slave labor becomes the basis for an ethical exhortation.
Consequence: Forced labor led to discouragement that blocked God's message.
Historical confirmation: The same oppression retold as a marker of identity.
Thematic parallel: Forced labor is repeated in Israel's own history under Solomon.
